headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: plano can feed broad networked outputs into transformers, while transformers can execute/write locally and amplify unverified content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: plano can emit network-fetched or API-derived content, and transformers can read files/stdin and run browser or shell-adjacent workflows. A shared handoff is plausible if plano output is copied into transformers inputs, so prompt injection is possible in default workflows, though not proven by direct integration.
conditions: IF plano output is pasted or piped into transformers prompts or example scripts
IF transformers treats external text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Strip HTML/markdown before passing outputs onward
Require manual review of plano outputs before reuse
Disable browser-driven ingestion for untrusted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: plano touches logs, traces, and metrics and has broad network egress; transformers can read and write the filesystem and send data to Hugging Face Hub or serve endpoints. If shared files or copied artifacts contain sensitive operational data, leakage can occur through either agent's normal I/O paths, though no shared workspace is documented.
conditions: IF logs, traces, or metrics from plano are placed in files readable by transformers
IF transformers uploads those files or derived text to a remote endpoint
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Redact logs and traces before handoff
Block outbound uploads from transformers for sensitive files
Review file permissions on shared directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: plano has out-of-process dataplane behavior and broad network egress, while transformers can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. If both operate on the same directory or project state, concurrent writes and side effects can collide; uncertainty remains because no locking or isolation is documented, so the higher severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or repository
IF transformers installs packages or rewrites files while plano is serving or routing traffic
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Run only one writer at a time
Mount shared paths read-only
Pin package versions before execution
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: plano can produce routed or transformed outputs that transformers may consume as model inputs or scripts. Because transformers can execute shell and write files, an unverified plano output can cascade into downstream actions or corrupted artifacts. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer high severity applies.
conditions: IF transformers uses plano-generated text as authoritative input
IF downstream scripts or files are produced from that unverified text
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before execution
Require schema validation on plano outputs
Log and diff all transformed artifacts
Disable auto-run of generated scripts
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The main compliance concern is operational logging: plano touches logs/traces/metrics, while transformers can persist files and send data to Hub or serve endpoints. Without a documented mismatch, only a low residual compliance risk is supported.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in plano logs, traces, or metrics
IF transformers persists or uploads that regulated data outside approved boundaries
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from logs
Set short retention on shared artifacts
Review upload destinations before use
Document data-class handling for both agents
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
